Package edu.cnu.mdi.log

Class FileLogger

java.lang.Object
edu.cnu.mdi.log.FileLogger
All Implemented Interfaces:
ILogListener, Closeable, AutoCloseable, EventListener
public class FileLogger extends Object implements ILogListener, Closeable
An ILogListener that appends log messages to a file with automatic size-based rotation.

File format

Messages are written as UTF-8 text, one entry per line (or one entry per block of lines for multi-line messages such as stack traces). Each entry is prefixed with an ISO-8601 date-time stamp and a fixed-width level tag: 

 2025-04-07T09:14:02 [INFO   ] Application started.
 2025-04-07T09:14:02 [CONFIG ] Loaded 195 countries from GeoJSON resource.
 2025-04-07T09:14:05 [WARNING] Configuration file not found; using defaults.

Unlike ConsoleLogger, the file logger uses a full date-time stamp (not just wall-clock time) so that entries from different days can be distinguished in a long-running application.

Rotation

When the log file exceeds getMaxFileSizeBytes() the current file is renamed to <name>.1 (overwriting any previous backup) and a fresh file is opened. This keeps exactly two files on disk at all times — the current log and one previous — which is sufficient for most desktop applications. More elaborate rotation strategies can be achieved by subclassing and overriding rotate().

The default maximum file size is 5 MB (5242880L bytes). An alternative limit can be supplied to the FileLogger(Path, long) constructor.

Flushing

The writer is flushed after every message. This is slightly less efficient than batched flushing but ensures that no messages are lost if the JVM terminates abnormally.

Registration

 Log.getInstance().addLogListener(new FileLogger(Path.of("app.log")));

Shutdown

FileLogger implements Closeable. In applications that want an orderly close of the underlying file, call close() during shutdown: 

 FileLogger fileLogger = new FileLogger(Path.of("app.log"));
 Log.getInstance().addLogListener(fileLogger);
 // ... application runs ...
 Log.getInstance().removeLogListener(fileLogger);
 fileLogger.close();

If close() is not called the file is closed when the JVM exits via a shutdown hook registered in the constructor, so no messages are silently dropped.

Thread safety

All write operations are synchronized on the FileLogger instance, so it is safe to receive messages from multiple threads simultaneously.

    • close

      public void close()
      Flush and close the underlying file writer.

      After this call the logger silently discards any further messages. The logger should also be unregistered from Log so it stops receiving messages: 

       Log.getInstance().removeLogListener(fileLogger);
 fileLogger.close();
      Specified by:
      close in interface AutoCloseable
      Specified by:
      close in interface Closeable
